title: Polymer clay galaxy swirl pendant
subtitle: A galaxy-effect pendant in swirled deep-blue, purple, and black with pearl
excerpt: A circular pendant about 35 mm across is built from swirled deep-blue, purple, and black polymer clay with pinches of pearl or white for star clusters. The colours are layered and twisted to create a galaxy spiral effect before the disc is cut and baked at 130°C for 30 minutes. A bail is attached before baking for a cord or chain.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles for polymer clay colour-swirl technique. Analogous to Skinner blend and mokume gane approaches in polymer clay practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A PVC-based modelling clay that sets hard in a domestic oven at 110-130°C; decorative only, not food-safe
Warming and kneading polymer clay by hand until soft and pliable before shaping
A colour technique where two or more colours are twisted together to create a marbled or spiral pattern without fully mixing the colours

content.text: A galaxy swirl pendant in
polymer clay

is a round disc 35 mm across and 4 mm thick, its face showing swirled deep-blue, purple, and black with scattered pearl highlights. The effect comes from a controlled partial mix of the colours: twisted together but not blended into a solid tone. A small bail pressed into the top edge before baking allows it to hang on a cord or chain. The disc bakes in a domestic oven at 130°C for 30 minutes.

materials.name: Small metal pendant bail (pre-made jewellery finding)
Fine cord or chain for wearing

tools.name: Pottery rolling pin (or smooth round object for rolling)
Needle tool (for piercing if no bail used)
Fettling knife (for cutting the disc shape)

content.text: Conditioning the clay
Work each colour separately first.
Conditioning
each colour for two minutes: roll between your palms, fold in half, and repeat until the clay folds without cracking. Cold or old polymer clay cracks at the fold until warmed through.
Creating the galaxy swirl

Roll each conditioned colour into a long rope about 8 mm in diameter. You will have three ropes: navy blue, purple, and black. Lay them side by side and twist them together with two or three full rotations to create a spiral log. This is the
swirl blend
base.
Fold the twisted log in half and twist again, then fold and twist once more. Stop before the colours merge into a solid tone: you want distinct spiral bands of each colour still visible.

Tear the pearl clay into small pinches and press them at random intervals into the surface of the twisted log. Roll the log gently between your palms once to press the pearl pieces in: they should partially blend to become small smears or clusters rather than solid balls.
Roll the entire log into a fat ball, then flatten it gently between your palms to a disc about 10 mm thick and 40 mm across.
Roll the disc flat with a rolling pin to 4 mm thickness. This spreads the swirl pattern across the face of the disc.
Cutting and finishing the disc

This pendant is a round polymer clay disc, 35 mm across and 4 mm thick. The face shows swirled deep-blue, purple, and black with scattered pearl highlights. The effect comes from a partial mix: the colours are twisted together but not fully blended. Press a small bail into the top edge before baking. This lets the pendant hang on a cord or chain. Bake the disc in a domestic oven at 130°C for 30 minutes.
Smooth the cut edge by rolling the disc between your palms very gently, just enough to round the sharp cut edge without distorting the face pattern.

Press a pre-made metal bail into the top edge of the disc with the loop portion above the disc edge. Press firmly until the bail base is flush with the disc surface. Pinch the clay around the bail base to hold it securely.
Alternative: if no bail is available, pierce a 3 mm hole with a needle tool at the top of the disc, 3 mm from the edge. Thread a jump ring through the hole after baking.
Baking

Place the pendant face-up on a ceramic tile or a piece of card on a baking tray. Bake in a domestic oven at 130°C for 30 minutes. Keep the kitchen ventilated during baking. Do not bake above 160°C. Allow to cool fully on the tile before handling: the pendant is slightly flexible when hot and sets rigid on cooling. The metal bail will be hot: use oven gloves.
Finishing after baking

The baked pendant surface can be left as-is for a soft matte finish. For a higher gloss and to bring out the depth of the swirl colours, wet-sand the face with 400-grit sandpaper followed by 800-grit, working under running water, then buff with a soft cloth. Apply a thin coat of liquid polymer clay varnish or clear nail polish for a glossy finish. Thread on a cord or chain.
Use and care

Baked polymer clay is durable for jewellery use but not food-safe. Keep the pendant away from food. Remove before swimming or prolonged contact with water: moisture does not damage the clay but may loosen a metal bail over time. Store flat or hanging to avoid scratching the face against other jewellery.
Variations
Use teal, forest green, and black for an ocean-depth palette instead of a galaxy palette. Add gold leaf flakes pressed onto the surface before baking for light scatter.
Cut the disc into a teardrop shape using the fettling knife for a different pendant silhouette, attaching the bail at the narrow pointed top.
Make three pendants at different sizes: 25 mm, 35 mm, and 45 mm, and wear them on graduated chain lengths as a layered set.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Swirl colours merge into a uniform dark colour
items.cause: The colours were twisted and folded too many times, fully blending rather than staying distinct
items.fix: Limit folding to three to four passes. Stop when the individual colour bands are still visible as distinct stripes. Start again with fresh clay if the current batch has over-mixed

items.problem: Bail pulls out of the disc after baking
items.cause: The bail base was not seated deeply enough into the clay, or the clay was not pressed firmly around the bail base
items.fix: Before baking, check the bail is fully pressed in with clay covering its base from both sides. If the bail pulls out after baking, reattach with two-part epoxy adhesive

items.problem: Disc warps or cups during baking
items.cause: The disc was placed on an uneven surface in the oven, or the clay was thicker on one side than the other
items.fix: Place the disc on a smooth ceramic tile (not on the oven rack directly). Roll the disc to an even 4 mm before cutting

items.problem: Surface looks dull and lifeless after baking
items.cause: Standard matte polymer clay does not develop gloss in the oven; the galaxy effect needs wet-sanding to bring out depth
items.fix: Wet-sand with 400 then 800 grit sandpaper under water, then buff with a soft cloth. Apply clear polymer varnish for a final gloss layer
